title: Grade 10 Science — Metals and Non-metals & Life Processes
description: Metals and Non-metals and Life Processes practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury (Hg) has a very low melting point of −38.83°C, making it the only metal that exists as a liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-metal that is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite (an allotrope of carbon, a non-metal) is a good conductor of electricity because its structure has free electrons that can move between layers.

questions.question: Metals are generally:
options: Good conductors of heat and electricity
questions.explanation: Metals are characterised by being good conductors of heat and electricity, having metallic lustre, and being malleable and ductile.

questions.question: The ore of aluminium is:
questions.explanation: Bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) is the principal ore of aluminium. Haematite is an iron ore, malachite contains copper, and magnetite is another iron ore.

questions.question: When sodium is exposed to air, it tarnishes quickly. The compound primarily formed is:
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts with oxygen in air to form sodium oxide (Na₂O) primarily, though Na₂O₂ can also form. This is why sodium is stored in kerosene.

questions.question: Which metal does not react with dilute acids but dissolves in aqua regia?
questions.explanation: Gold is below hydrogen in the activity series and does not react with dilute acids. However, aqua regia (3 parts HCl + 1 part HNO₃) dissolves gold.

questions.question: Thermite reaction: 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe. What does this demonstrate?
options: Iron is more reactive than aluminium
Aluminium is more reactive than iron
questions.explanation: Aluminium displaces iron from its oxide because aluminium is more reactive. This is an example of a highly exothermic displacement reaction used in welding railway tracks.

questions.question: The process of depositing a layer of a desired metal on another metal using electricity is called:
questions.explanation: Electroplating uses electricity to coat one metal with a thin layer of another metal. It is used to prevent corrosion and improve appearance.

questions.question: The process by which plants manufacture food from sunlight, water, and CO₂ is called:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which chlorophyll-containing plants use sunlight, water, and CO₂ to produce glucose and oxygen.

questions.question: Where does the digestion of proteins begin in the human body?
questions.explanation: Protein digestion begins in the stomach where pepsin (activated by HCl) starts breaking down proteins into smaller peptides.

questions.question: The enzyme secreted by salivary glands that acts on starch is:
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) is secreted by salivary glands. It begins the digestion of starch into maltose in the mouth.

questions.question: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from:
questions.explanation: During the light reactions of photosynthesis, water molecules are split (photolysis). The oxygen atoms are released as O₂ gas.

questions.question: Amoeba takes in food through a process called:
questions.explanation: Amoeba engulfs food particles by wrapping its pseudopodia around them. This process of engulfing solid particles is called phagocytosis, a type of endocytosis.

questions.question: Stomata open when guard cells:
questions.explanation: When guard cells absorb water, they become turgid and curved, pulling away from each other to open the stomatal pore. Flaccid guard cells close the stoma.

questions.question: In the kidney, the process of removing waste from blood is called:
questions.explanation: In the glomerulus, blood is filtered under high pressure. This process is called ultrafiltration — small molecules including urea, glucose, and water pass through, while large proteins and blood cells remain.
